newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk secularist PM says to fight Islamist activism.
newsitem.headline: Turk secularist PM says to fight Islamist activism.

text.p: Turkey's new secularist Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz said on Wednesday his anti-Islamist coalition would continue a fight launched by the military against religious activism.
"Our government will give fundamentalism no breathing space," Yilmaz told members of his Motherland Party at a meeting in parliament.

President Suleyman Demirel appointed Yilmaz prime minister on Monday at the head of a secularist coalition aimed at putting an end to months of conflict between the outgoing Islamist-led government and the army.
Prime minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned last month under pressure from the staunchly secularist generals, who began a campaign against the rising profile of Islamists in February.
Yilmaz blamed Erbakan's Welfare Party for sparking the religious revival. "They are the ones who incited fundamentalism," he said.
Yilmaz cautioned Erbakan over his strong objections to his appointment.
"We are warning Erbakan. He is playing with fire...The aggressive stance which he has adopted since losing his post is the biggest obstacle in the way of (Turkey's) 65 million people," he said.
Erbakan had attacked Demirel's decision to give Yilmaz the task of forming a government rather than choosing an alliance including the Islamists and their conservative coalition partners.
Welfare is facing the prospect of closure in a constitutional court case alleging that the party threatened NATO member Turkey's secular system.
